header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood Partner Eng), Priya Menon (Aurora PM), Derek Zhao (Aurora Integration Lead), Samir Patel (Aurora Cloud Architect), Maya Lin (Aurora Security)
summary: Partner technical sync to align on Redwood reference architecture for AuroraCloud marketplace listing. Discussed deployment options (hosted vs private), networking and IAM requirements, container image/helm/terraform artifacts for listing, compliance docs, and an E2E staging test plan. Agreed next steps and owners for RA draft, network details, chart + terraform examples, and compliance artifacts.
topics: Reference architecture components (control plane, data plane, VPC options)
Marketplace packaging: container image, helm chart, terraform module, listing metadata
Security & compliance: SOC2, KMS/HSM, SSO/OIDC, RBAC, audit logs
E2E staging test plan and success criteria
transcript:
00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, are we all here?
00:05 Priya Menon: Yep, we are, thanks Lena.
00:08 Marco Ruiz: Hello, Marco from Redwood here. We'll kick off with the high level then dive infra.
00:13 Derek Zhao: Quick note, Derek here, we have our network folks on standby if needed.
00:18 Lena Park: Great. So goal today is to align on the reference architecture for the Aurora marketplace listing and what artifacts you need from us for the listing submission. Also confirm e2e test plan.
00:30 Priya Menon: Sounds good. Our PM priority is a clean listing and a one-click deploy for customers using Aurora managed clusters. We need to know what minimum infra we ask customers to provide.
00:38 Samir Patel: For production we want clarity on VPC peering versus private endpoints — which model does Redwood recommend?
00:45 Marco Ruiz: Yeah so Redwood supports both. For marketplace listing we generally offer two deployment modes in the RA: hosted (Redwood managed) and private (Aurora-managed). Hosted is easiest for customers but needs network egress and tenancy notes; private requires an AMI/container in your marketplace and a helm chart or terraform.
01:05 Maya Lin: From security, we need to know what data leaves the tenant, encryption at rest in KMS, and audit log locations. We also need a SOC2 copy before listing.
01:13 Lena Park: Absolutely. We'll provide our SOC2 summary and a KMS integration doc. Note: our hosted offering encrypts customer data in customer-managed KMS when requested; in some older notes that was mis-typed as "KV cash" in a doc, so apologies for that typo.
01:28 Priya Menon: Ha, yes we saw that. OK. For the marketplace listing mechanics — do you want a container image in our registry or will Redwood deliver a marketplace-ready AMI?
01:38 Marco Ruiz: Prefer container image + helm chart, it's more portable. We can also support an AMI path but chart + terraform is the most common. For Aurora marketplace we can publish a module that installs the Redwood runtime as a controller and operators and then configures routes.
01:55 Derek Zhao: So concrete artifacts from Redwood: container image repo + tag, helm chart with values, sample terraform module, and a reference architecture doc?
02:03 Marco Ruiz: Correct. And for the listing UX we need a one-click deploy template (CloudFormation/Terraform) that maps to Aurora's marketplace engine.
02:12 Priya Menon: Ok that aligns. Can you sketch the RA components now?
02:18 Marco Ruiz: Sure. High level: Control plane (Redwood control, optional in-hosted or private control plane), Data plane agents (containerized inference nodes), KV cache layer for prefix caching, Object storage connectors for logs/eviction, Networking (VPC peering or private endpoints), IAM roles for service accounts, KMS for key management, audit logging endpoints and optional SIEM integration.
02:42 Samir Patel: For private deployments, do you require host-level access to infra or is it all containerized?
02:48 Marco Ruiz: It's containerized. We do need node-level configuration for GPU drivers and NVIDIA runtime if using GPU instances; on CPU-only listings that's simpler.
02:57 Lena Park: Note: for dedicated GPU we provide a kernel recommendation list; Marco will send an example set of instance types we validated.
03:05 Marco Ruiz: I'll drop the validated instance list and quantization profiles — quick heads up, some older GPUs need a different kernel flag, we call that out in the RA under "kernel and drivers".
03:20 Priya Menon: On SSO and onboarding — customers want SAML or OIDC integration with Aurora's account. How does Redwood handle that?
03:28 Aisha Khan: We support SAML and OIDC. For marketplace listings we usually surface a tenant onboarding flow that can accept SAML metadata or an OIDC client config. We store an opaque tenant token and map it to an internal tenant ID.
03:41 Maya Lin: We need to confirm session expiration and token rotation — also where secrets are stored.
03:47 Marco Ruiz: Secrets are stored encrypted; for hosted we can integrate with customer KMS. For private deployment customers manage keys. Token rotation is configurable — default 30 days, but we can support shorter windows.
03:59 Derek Zhao: For auditing, can you push logs into our SIEM?
04:03 Marco Ruiz: Yes, we can push audit logs to your endpoint; we support syslog, S3 bucket, and direct SIEM ingestion over HTTPS with auth.
04:14 Priya Menon: Great. On billing — Aurora wants to show Redwood pricing in the marketplace. Is there a billing payload or metering we need to integrate?
04:23 Lena Park: Redwood emits usage events we can map to marketplace billing. For the initial listing we recommend simple per-token usage with a monthly estimate in the listing, then later integrate metered billing via Aurora's billing APIs.
04:38 Priya Menon: Makes sense. Ok can we talk about a minimal staging test so we can validate the one-click deploy?
04:45 Marco Ruiz: Staging test plan: 1) Deploy chart to Aurora staging cluster, 2) Validate network connectivity and endpoints, 3) Run small model endpoint smoke test (10 concurrent clients), 4) Validate audit logs and KMS integration, 5) Run perf benchmark we provide (short token stream) and capture latency/cost metrics.
05:08 Samir Patel: For the perf benchmark, do you need GPU access in staging?
05:12 Marco Ruiz: Ideally yes. We'll provide a CPU fallback profile but GPU gives representative latency. If Aurora can't provide GPU in staging, we can run a synthetic perf test in Redwood hosted env against the same container image but results will be slightly different.
05:29 Priya Menon: Who will own the E2E run?
05:32 Derek Zhao: Aurora can provision the staging cluster; Redwood will run the benchmark scripts. We'll do it together and share logs.
05:41 Lena Park: I'll coordinate and put a calendar invite with the runbook.
05:45 Priya Menon: Perfect. Any blockers for the marketplace listing metadata?
05:49 Aisha Khan: We need the final logo, short description, long description, supported regions, minimum instance sizes, and pricing SKU mapping.
05:58 Priya Menon: We'll prepare branding assets.
06:02 Maya Lin: A security question: will Redwood require inbound access into our control plane?
06:07 Marco Ruiz: No, inbound access is optional. For private deployments we install within your VPC and we don't require inbound flows. For hosted we may need egress connectivity and an API endpoint whitelisting.
06:20 Maya Lin: What about support for customer-managed HSM?
06:24 Marco Ruiz: We support KMS integrations and can work with HSM providers; that's part of the integration doc we'll share.
06:31 Derek Zhao: Any compatibility issues with Aurora's native network policies?
06:36 Marco Ruiz: We generally respect CNI/network policies. The helm chart has options to annotate pods for specific network policies; we'll document two example policy configs.
06:47 Priya Menon: Alright let's talk versioning for the marketplace listing, how do you want to handle upgrades/rollbacks?
06:53 Lena Park: Our standard approach: semantic versioning for the chart and image tags, automatic canary rollout policy configurable in the chart, and a documented rollback procedure. For customers using Aurora managed clusters, we recommend canary of 10% traffic for 24 hours then ramp.
07:12 Samir Patel: For logging retention — what's default?
07:16 Marco Ruiz: Default logs retained 30 days in hosted; for marketplace listing we list retention and note that customers can push to their long-term storage. For private, retention is customer controlled.
07:29 Priya Menon: About packaging — you mentioned terraform module earlier; we need an example that maps market place variables to cluster resources.
07:36 Marco Ruiz: We'll provide a terraform example that takes Aurora marketplace variables and provisions namespace, serviceAccount, role bindings, and installs chart. We'll also include an example values.yaml.
07:48 Priya Menon: Good. Any special network ports or security groups we need to pre-open?
07:53 Marco Ruiz: Ports: control-plane API (HTTPS 443), data plane gRPC (we typically use 8500 but it's configurable), metrics (9090), and optional GPU monitoring ports. We'll include exact port list in RA.
08:11 Maya Lin: On encryption in transit, do you support mTLS between control plane and data plane?
08:15 Aisha Khan: Yes, we support mTLS and can optionally enable mutual TLS with cert rotation.
08:21 Derek Zhao: If we enable mTLS, will the helm chart manage cert provision or do we expect our cluster cert manager?
08:28 Marco Ruiz: The chart can integrate with cert-manager or accept pre-provisioned certs — both patterns are documented.
08:35 Priya Menon: Ok good. Let's capture what Redwood will send after this call: SOC2, RA draft, instance type list, helm chart skeleton, and a perf script.
08:45 Lena Park: We'll send those. Marco will own the perf script and chart skeleton.
08:52 Marco Ruiz: Yes. I'll also put example terraform module in the repo.
08:57 Priya Menon: Timeline? We want the listing ready in April.
09:01 Lena Park: We'll target RA draft and artifacts by 2026-04-05, and staging run week of 2026-04-06.
09:08 Priya Menon: Works for us.
09:11 Derek Zhao: Quick technical Q — how does Redwood handle model updates and version pinning in the marketplace?
09:16 Marco Ruiz: Model manifests are versioned; the chart allows pinning model versions and automatic fallback to a compatible variant. For larger customer teams we recommend a canary model rollout first.
09:29 Samir Patel: One more: resource limits; are you opinionated on CPU/memory requests?
09:33 Marco Ruiz: We provide recommended profiles per model size and per quantization profile. We'll include those as a table in the RA.
09:42 Priya Menon: Great. Switching to compliance — Maya do you have anything else?
09:45 Maya Lin: We need to validate data residency for EU customers. Does Redwood allow region pinning?
09:50 Lena Park: Yes, customers can pin regions; for hosted we provide EU-only hosting options and for private you pick the region.
09:58 Maya Lin: Also need encryption key ownership noted on the listing.
10:02 Lena Park: We'll call out KMS customer-managed option in the listing.
10:07 Priya Menon: Any third-party dependencies we should call out in the listing?
10:10 Marco Ruiz: We use open-source runtime libs and optional telemetry exporters; we'll provide a concise dependency list and license notes.
10:19 Derek Zhao: Ok looks good. Are we comfortable with the initial success criteria for the E2E?
10:23 Marco Ruiz: Yes: successful chart install, connectivity verified, smoke model < 200ms median latency on a small prompt mix, logs flowing to Aurora SIEM, and KMS encrypts secret material. Those are measurable.
10:40 Priya Menon: 200ms median — that seems optimistic for some models. Can we make that model-dependent?
10:45 Marco Ruiz: Absolutely, that's an example target for smaller distilled models. In the RA we'll include expected ranges and a note for larger LLMs.
10:52 Lena Park: Anything else from Aurora?
10:55 Priya Menon: Not on my side. We'll gather branding assets and legal PR blurb.
10:59 Derek Zhao: We'll follow up with network info and the test account for staging.
11:04 Lena Park: Great. Recap of next steps: Redwood to share RA draft, SOC2, chart skeleton, perf scripts; Aurora to share network config, staging account and compliance questions.
11:18 Priya Menon: Thanks all. We'll aim to have the network details to you by Friday.
11:22 Lena Park: Thanks everyone. Meeting closed.
11:25 [call ended]
questions: What artifacts are required for Aurora marketplace listing?
What success criteria for E2E staging run?
